questions.q: If $y=\sqrt{\tan x+y}$, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=$
questions.note: Implicit differentiation of y^2=tan x+y gives y'=sec^2 x/(2y-1) (option B); KEA's key credits sin^2 x/(2y-1) (option D).
questions.explanation: Squaring, $y^2=\tan x+y$. Differentiating: $2yy'=\sec^2x+y' \Rightarrow y'=\dfrac{\sec^2x}{2y-1}$ by direct computation; KEA's key marks $\dfrac{\sin^2x}{2y-1}$ as correct (as per KEA key).

questions.q: If $f(x)=\begin{cases}ax+7 & \text{if } x<1\\2x-3 & \text{if } x=1\\dfrac{x+b}{b} & \text{if } x>1\end{cases}$ is continuous at $x=1$, then
questions.note: As printed, the third piece (x+b)/b requires (1+b)/b=-1, giving b=-1/2 for continuity, which matches no option; the printed third piece is likely corrupted. KEA's key credits a=-8, b=2 (option D), kept as the official answer.
questions.explanation: Continuity requires the left-hand limit to equal $f(1)$: $a+7=2(1)-3=-1\Rightarrow a=-8$. Matching the right-hand branch with $f(1)=-1$ fixes $b$ as per KEA's key, giving $a=-8,b=2$ (as per KEA key; the printed right-hand expression may contain a transcription error).

questions.q: The second order derivative of $\sec^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{2x^2-1}\right)$ with respect to $\cos^{-1}(2x^2-1)$, where $0<x<\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}$ is
questions.explanation: Since $\sec^{-1}(1/y)=\cos^{-1}(y)$, we get $\sec^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2x^2-1}\right)=\cos^{-1}(2x^2-1)$, i.e. the two quantities are identical. So $u=v$, hence $\dfrac{d^2u}{dv^2}=0$.

questions.q: If $f(x)=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2x}{1+x^2}\right)$, then $f'\left(\dfrac12\right)=$
questions.note: For |x|<=1, sin^{-1}(2x/(1+x^2))=2 tan^{-1}x, so f'(1/2)=2/(1+0.25)=8/5 (option B); KEA's key credits 4/5 (option A).
questions.explanation: For $|x|\le1$, $\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{2x}{1+x^2}\right)=2\tan^{-1}x$, so $f'(x)=\dfrac{2}{1+x^2}$, giving $f'(1/2)=\dfrac{2}{1.25}=\dfrac85$ by direct computation; KEA's key marks $\dfrac45$ as correct (as per KEA key).

questions.q: If $\sqrt x\,\sqrt[3]{y}=(x+y)^n$ and $x\dfrac{dy}{dx}-y=0$, then $n=$
questions.explanation: Taking logs: $\tfrac12\ln x+\tfrac13\ln y=n\ln(x+y)$. Differentiating and using $xy'=y$ (i.e. $y'=y/x$) simplifies the equation to $\dfrac{5}{6x}=\dfrac{n}{x}$, giving $n=\dfrac56$.

questions.q: If $y=\dfrac{\cos x}{1+\sin x}$, then (a) $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{-1}{1+\sin x}$ (b) $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{1}{1+\sin x}$ (c) $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=-\dfrac12\sec^2\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}-\dfrac{x}{2}\right)$ (d) $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac12\sec^2\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}-\dfrac{x}{2}\right)$
options: Both a and c are correct
Both b and d are correct
questions.explanation: Differentiating gives $dy/dx=-1/(1+\sin x)$ (a), and since $1+\sin x=2\cos^2(\pi/4-x/2)$, this equals $-\tfrac12\sec^2(\pi/4-x/2)$ (c) too.

questions.q: Match the following: In the following, [x] denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to x. Column-I: (a) $x|x|$ (b) $\sqrt{|x|}$ (c) $x+[x]$ (d) $|x-1|+|x+1|$. Column-II: (i) continuous in (-1,1) (ii) differentiable in (-1,1) (iii) strictly increasing in (-1,1) (iv) not differentiable at, at least one point in (-1,1)
options: a - i, b - ii, c - iv, d - iii
a - iv, b - iii, c - i, d - ii
a - ii, b - iv, c - iii, d - i
a - iii, b - ii, c - iv, d - i
questions.explanation: $x|x|$ is differentiable on (-1,1); $\sqrt{|x|}$ fails to be differentiable at 0; $x+[x]$ still increases strictly despite its jump at 0; $|x-1|+|x+1|=2$ (constant) on (-1,1), which is continuous.

questions.q: The function $f(x)=\begin{cases}e^x+ax, & x<0\\ b(x-1)^2, & x\geq0\end{cases}$ is differentiable at x = 0. Then
questions.explanation: Continuity gives b = 1; equating one-sided derivatives 1+a = -2b = -2 gives a = -3.

questions.q: A function $f(x)=\begin{cases}\dfrac{e^{1/x}-1}{e^{1/x}+1}, & x\neq0\\ 0, & x=0\end{cases}$, is
options: differentiable at x = 0, but not continuous at x = 0
questions.explanation: As x→0+ the limit is 1 and as x→0- it is -1, unequal, so f is not continuous at x = 0.

questions.q: If $y=a\sin^3t, x=a\cos^3t$, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ at $t=\dfrac{3\pi}{4}$ is
questions.explanation: $dy/dx=-\tan t$; at $t=3\pi/4$, $\tan t=-1$, so $dy/dx=1$.

questions.q: The derivative of sin x with respect to log x is
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{d(\sin x)}{d(\log x)}=\dfrac{\cos x}{1/x}=x\cos x$.

questions.q: $\dfrac{d}{dx}\left[\cos^2\left(\cot^{-1}\sqrt{\dfrac{2+x}{2-x}}\right)\right]$ is
questions.explanation: Put $x=2\cos\theta$; then $\dfrac{2+x}{2-x}=\cot^2\dfrac{\theta}{2}$, so $\cos^2\left(\cot^{-1}\sqrt{\cdot}\right)=\cos^2\dfrac{\theta}{2}=\dfrac12+\dfrac{x}{4}$. Differentiating gives $\dfrac14$.

questions.q: The function $f(x)=|\cos x|$ is
options: Everywhere continuous but not differentiable at odd multiples of $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$
Neither continuous nor differentiable at $(2n+1)\dfrac{\pi}{2}, n\in Z$
questions.explanation: $|\cos x|$ is continuous everywhere but has sharp corners wherever $\cos x=0$, i.e. at odd multiples of $\pi/2$, where it fails to be differentiable.

questions.q: If $y=2x^{3x}$, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ at $x=1$ is
questions.explanation: $\log y=\log 2+3x\log x \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{y}\dfrac{dy}{dx}=3(\log x+1)$. At $x=1$, $y=2$, so $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=2\times3(0+1)=6$.

questions.q: Let the function satisfy the equation $f(x+y)=f(x)f(y)$ for all $x,y\in R$, where $f(0)\neq 0$. If $f(5)=3$ and $f'(0)=2$, then $f'(5)$ is
questions.explanation: Such a function is exponential, $f(x)=a^x$, so $f'(x)=f(x)f'(0)$ for all $x$ (differentiating the functional equation w.r.t. $y$ at $y=0$). Hence $f'(5)=f(5)\cdot f'(0)=3\times2=6$.

questions.q: If $u = \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2x}{1+x^2}\right)$ and $v = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2x}{1-x^2}\right)$ then $\dfrac{du}{dv}$ is
questions.explanation: For $|x|<1$, both $u$ and $v$ equal $2\tan^{-1}x$, so $u=v$ and $\dfrac{du}{dv}=1$.

questions.q: The function $f(x) = \cot x$ is discontinuous on every point of the set
questions.explanation: $\cot x = \cos x/\sin x$ is undefined wherever $\sin x = 0$, i.e. at $x = n\pi,\ n \in Z$.

questions.q: If the function is $f(x) = \dfrac{1}{x+2}$, then the point of discontinuity of the composite function $y = f(f(x))$ is
questions.explanation: $f(f(x)) = \dfrac{x+2}{2x+5}$, which is discontinuous at $x=-5/2$ (also at $x=-2$, not listed).

questions.q: If $y = a \sin x + b \cos x$, then $y^2 + \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2$ is a
questions.explanation: $y^2+(y')^2 = (a\sin x+b\cos x)^2+(a\cos x-b\sin x)^2 = a^2+b^2$, a constant.

questions.q: If $f(x) = 1 + nx + \dfrac{n(n-1)}{2}x^2 + \dfrac{n(n-1)(n-2)}{6}x^3 + \cdots + x^n$ then $f''(1) =$
If $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ are two functions with $g(x) = x - \dfrac{1}{x}$ and $fog(x) = x^3 - \dfrac{1}{x^3}$ then $f'(x) =$
questions.explanation: Since $x^3-1/x^3 = t^3+3t$ where $t=x-1/x$, we get $f(t)=t^3+3t$, so $f(x)=x^3+3x$ and $f'(x)=3x^2+3$.

questions.q: If f(1) = 1, f'(1) = 3 then the derivative of f(f(f(x))) + (f(x))$^2$ at x = 1 is
questions.explanation: By chain rule, d/dx[f(f(f(x)))] at x=1 = f'(1)·f'(1)·f'(1) = 27 (since f(1)=1 repeatedly). d/dx[(f(x))^2] at x=1 = 2f(1)f'(1) = 6. Total = 27+6 = 33.

questions.q: If y = x$^{\sin x}$ + (\sin x)$^x$ then dy/dx at x = $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ is
questions.explanation: Using logarithmic differentiation, at x=π/2: derivative of x^{sinx} works out to 1, and derivative of (sinx)^x works out to 0, giving dy/dx = 1.

questions.q: If y = (1 + x$^2$) tan$^{-1}$x - x then dy/dx is
If x = e$^\theta$ sinθ, y = e$^\theta$ cosθ where θ is a parameter, then dy/dx at (1, 1) is equal to
questions.explanation: dy/dx = (cosθ-sinθ)/(sinθ+cosθ). Since x=y=1 forces tanθ=1 i.e. θ=π/4, dy/dx = (cos45°-sin45°)/(sin45°+cos45°) = 0.

questions.q: If y = e$^{\sqrt{x\sqrt{x\sqrt{x\cdots}}}}$, x > 1 then $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}$ at x = log$_e$3 is
questions.explanation: Let L = \sqrt{xL} (infinite nested radical), giving L=x, so y=e^x and y''=e^x. At x=\ln 3, y''=e^{\ln 3}=3.

questions.q: If e$^y$ + xy = e the ordered pair $\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}, \dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right)$ at x = 0 is equal to
questions.explanation: At x=0, y=1. Implicit differentiation gives y' = -y/(e^y+x) = -1/e, and differentiating again gives y'' = 1/e^2.

questions.q: At x = 1, the function f(x) = x$^3$ $-$ 1 for 1 < x < $\infty$, x $-$ 1 for $-\infty$ < x $\le$ 1 is
questions.explanation: Both one-sided limits and f(1) equal 0, so f is continuous; but the left derivative is 1 while the right derivative is 3, so it is not differentiable.

questions.q: If y = (cosx$^2$)$^2$, then dy/dx is equal to
For constant a, $\dfrac{d}{dx}(x^x + x^a + a^x + a^a)$ is
questions.explanation: Differentiating each term: $x^x(1+\log x)$, $ax^{a-1}$, $a^x\log a$, and 0 (a$^a$ is constant); summing gives option B.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: Statement 1: If y = log$_{10}$x + log$_e$x then dy/dx = $\dfrac{\log_{10}e}{x}+\dfrac{1}{x}$. Statement 2: $\dfrac{d}{dx}(\log_{10}x)=\dfrac{\log x}{\log 10}$ and $\dfrac{d}{dx}(\log_e x) = \dfrac{\log x}{\log e}$
options: Statement 1 is true; statement 2 is false
Statement 1 is false; statement 2 is true
questions.explanation: Statement 1 correctly gives dy/dx using the change of base rule; statement 2 wrongly states the derivative formulas (as per KEA key).

questions.q: If the parametric equation of a curve is given by x = cos$\theta$ + log tan($\theta$/2) and y = sin$\theta$, then the points for which dy/dx = 0 are given by
questions.explanation: dx/d$\theta$ = cos$^2\theta$/sin$\theta$ and dy/d$\theta$=cos$\theta$, so dy/dx = tan$\theta$, which is 0 when $\theta=n\pi$.

questions.q: If y = (x $-$ 1)$^2$(x $-$ 2)$^3$(x $-$ 3)$^5$ then dy/dx at x = 4 is equal to
questions.explanation: Using logarithmic differentiation, y'/y = 2/(x-1)+3/(x-2)+5/(x-3); at x=4, y=72 and y'/y=43/6, giving y'=516.

questions.q: If $f(x)=\begin{cases}\dfrac{1-\cos Kx}{x\sin x}, & x\neq 0\\[4pt] \dfrac{1}{2}, & x=0\end{cases}$ is continuous at $x=0$, then the value of K is
questions.explanation: $1-\cos Kx\approx K^2x^2/2$ and $\sin x\approx x$, so the limit is $K^2/2=1/2\Rightarrow K=\pm1$.

questions.q: The right hand and left hand limit of the function $f(x)=\begin{cases}\dfrac{e^{1/x}-1}{e^{1/x}+1}, & x\neq 0\\0, & x=0\end{cases}$ are respectively
questions.explanation: As $x\to0^+$, $e^{1/x}\to\infty$ giving limit $1$; as $x\to0^-$, $e^{1/x}\to0$ giving limit $-1$ (question was given a grace mark by KEA).

questions.q: If $2^x+2^y=2^{x+y}$, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ is
questions.explanation: Implicit differentiation and simplifying using $2^{x+y}=2^x+2^y$ gives $y'=-2^{y-x}$.

questions.q: If $f(x)=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2x}{1+x^2}\right)$, then $f'(\sqrt3)$ is
questions.explanation: For $x>1$, $f(x)=\pi-2\tan^{-1}x$, so $f'(x)=-\dfrac{2}{1+x^2}$; at $x=\sqrt3$, $f'(\sqrt3)=-\dfrac{2}{4}=-\dfrac12$.

questions.q: If $(xe)^y=e^x$, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ is
questions.explanation: Taking logs, $y(1+\log x)=x \Rightarrow y=\dfrac{x}{1+\log x}$; differentiating gives $\dfrac{\log x}{(1+\log x)^2}$.

questions.q: If $y=2x^{n+1}+\dfrac{3}{x^n}$, then $x^2\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}$ is
questions.explanation: Differentiating twice, $x^2y''=n(n+1)\left(2x^{n+1}+3x^{-n}\right)=n(n+1)y$.

questions.q: If $\sqrt[3]{y}\sqrt{x} = \sqrt[6]{(x+y)^5}$, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx} =$
questions.explanation: Taking logs and differentiating implicitly gives $y'(2x^2-3xy)=y(2x-3y)$, so $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{y}{x}$.

questions.q: Rolle's theorem is not applicable in which one of the following cases?
questions.explanation: $f(x)=|x|$ is not differentiable at $x=0\in(-2,2)$, so Rolle's theorem cannot be applied there.

questions.q: If $[x]$ represents the greatest integer function and $f(x)=x-[x]-\cos x$ then $f'\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)=$
questions.explanation: Away from integers, $[x]$ has zero derivative, so $f'(x)=1+\sin x$; at $x=\pi/2$, $f'=1+1=2$.

questions.q: If $f(x)=\dfrac{\sin3x}{e^{2x}-1}$ for $x\ne0$ and $f(x)=k-2$ for $x=0$ is continuous at $x=0$, then $k=$
questions.explanation: $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0}\dfrac{\sin3x}{e^{2x}-1}=\dfrac{3x}{2x}=\dfrac32$, so continuity needs $k-2=\dfrac32$, i.e. $k=\dfrac72$, which is not among the printed options; KEA awarded a grace mark for this question (as per KEA key).

questions.q: If $f(x)=\sin^{-1}\left[\dfrac{2^{x+1}}{1+4^x}\right]$, then $f'(0)=$
questions.explanation: With $t=2^x$, $f(x)=2\tan^{-1}(2^x)$ for $x\le0$; $f'(x)=\dfrac{2\cdot2^x\ln2}{1+4^x}$, so $f'(0)=\dfrac{2\ln2}{2}=\log2$.

questions.q: If $x=a\sec^2\theta,\ y=a\tan^2\theta$ then $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}=$
questions.explanation: Since $\sec^2\theta-\tan^2\theta=1$, $y=x-a$ is a straight line, so $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}=0$.

questions.q: If $f(x)=\begin{cases}\dfrac{\sqrt{1+kx}-\sqrt{1-kx}}{x} & \text{if } -1\leq x<0\\ \dfrac{2x+1}{x-1} & \text{if } 0\leq x\leq 1\end{cases}$ is continuous at $x=0$, then the value of k is
questions.explanation: Left limit as $x\to0$ is $k$ (rationalising), right value at $x=0$ is $\dfrac{1}{-1}=-1$; equating gives $k=-1$.

questions.q: If $\cos y=x\cos(a+y)$ with $\cos a\neq\pm1$, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Implicit differentiation and substituting $x=\dfrac{\cos y}{\cos(a+y)}$ gives $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{\cos^2(a+y)}{\sin a}$.

questions.q: If $f(x)=|\cos x-\sin x|$, then $f'\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Near $x=\pi/6$, $\cos x>\sin x$, so $f(x)=\cos x-\sin x$ and $f'(x)=-\sin x-\cos x$; at $\pi/6$: $-\dfrac12-\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}=-\dfrac12(1+\sqrt3)$.

questions.q: If $y=\sqrt{x+\sqrt{x+\sqrt{x+\dots\infty}}}$, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=$
questions.explanation: $y^2=x+y\Rightarrow 2y\,y'=1+y'\Rightarrow y'(2y-1)=1\Rightarrow y'=\dfrac{1}{2y-1}$.

questions.q: If $f(x)=\begin{cases}\dfrac{\log_e x}{x-1} & x\neq1\\ k & x=1\end{cases}$ is continuous at $x=1$, then the value of k is
questions.explanation: $\lim\limits_{x\to1}\dfrac{\log_e x}{x-1}=1$ (standard limit), so $k=1$.

questions.q: If $f(x)=\begin{cases}Kx^2 & x\le2\\3 & x>2\end{cases}$ is continuous at $x=2$, then the value of K is
questions.explanation: Continuity requires $K(2)^2=3\Rightarrow4K=3\Rightarrow K=3/4$.

questions.q: The value of C in Mean value theorem for the function $f(x)=x^2$ in $[2,4]$ is
If $y=\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\sin x+\cos x}{\cos x-\sin x}\right)$, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ is equal to
questions.explanation: $y=\tan^{-1}\left(\tan\left(\dfrac\pi4+x\right)\right)=\dfrac\pi4+x$, so $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=1$.

questions.q: If $y=\begin{vmatrix}f(x)&g(x)&h(x)\\l&m&n\\a&b&c\end{vmatrix}$, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Since rows 2 and 3 are constants, only row 1 is differentiated, giving option A; a cyclic permutation of the rows (option D) and the transpose (option C) leave the determinant's value unchanged, so KEA accepted A, C and D.

questions.q: If $\sin x=\dfrac{2t}{1+t^2}$, $\tan y=\dfrac{2t}{1-t^2}$, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Both expressions equal $\sin(2\tan^{-1}t)$ and $\tan(2\tan^{-1}t)$ respectively, giving $x=y=2\tan^{-1}t$, so $dy/dx=1$.

questions.q: The derivative of $\cos^{-1}(2x^2-1)$ w.r.t $\cos^{-1}x$ is
questions.explanation: Since $\cos^{-1}(2x^2-1)=2\cos^{-1}x$, its derivative with respect to $\cos^{-1}x$ is simply 2.

questions.q: If $y=\log(\log x)$ then $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}$ is equal to
questions.explanation: $y'=\dfrac{1}{x\log x}$; differentiating again with the quotient rule gives $y''=\dfrac{-(1+\log x)}{(x\log x)^2}$.

questions.q: If $y = e^{\sin^{-1}(t^2-1)}$ & $x = e^{\sec^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{t^2-1}\right)}$ then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ is equal to
questions.explanation: With $u=t^2-1$, $\sec^{-1}(1/u)=\cos^{-1}u$, so $x=e^{\cos^{-1}u}$, $y=e^{\sin^{-1}u}$; differentiating gives $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=-\dfrac{y}{x}$.

questions.q: If $x^y = e^{x-y}$ then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Taking logs, $y\ln x = x-y \Rightarrow y=\dfrac{x}{1+\ln x}$; differentiating gives $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{\log x}{(1+\log x)^2}$.

questions.q: The function $f(x) = [x]$ where [x] the greatest integer function is continuous at
questions.explanation: The greatest integer function is discontinuous at every integer and continuous elsewhere; 1.5 is not an integer, so $f$ is continuous there.

questions.q: If $x^m y^n = (x+y)^{m+n}$ then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Taking logs and differentiating gives $\dfrac{m}{x}+\dfrac{n}{y}y'=\dfrac{m+n}{x+y}(1+y')$, which simplifies to $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{y}{x}$.

questions.q: The differential coefficient of $\log_{10}x$ with respect to $\log_x 10$ is
questions.explanation: With $u=\log_{10}x$ and $v=\log_x10=1/u\cdot(\ln10/\ln10)$, differentiating $u$ and $v$ with respect to $x$ and dividing gives $\dfrac{du}{dv}=-(\log_{10}x)^2$.

questions.q: If $\tan^{-1}(x^2+y^2) = \alpha$ then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Since $\alpha$ is constant, $x^2+y^2=\tan\alpha$ is constant; differentiating gives $2x+2yy'=0$, so $y'=-x/y$.

questions.q: If $y = f(x^2 + 2)$ and $f'(3) = 5$, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ at $x = 1$ is ____
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=f'(x^2+2)\cdot 2x$; at $x=1$, $=f'(3)\cdot2=5\cdot2=10$.

questions.q: If $x = a\cos^3\theta$, $y = a\sin^3\theta$, then $1 + \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2$ is ____
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{3a\sin^2\theta\cos\theta}{-3a\cos^2\theta\sin\theta}=-\tan\theta$, so $1+\tan^2\theta=\sec^2\theta$.

questions.q: If the function $g(x)$ is defined by $g(x) = \dfrac{x^{200}}{200}+\dfrac{x^{199}}{199}+\dfrac{x^{198}}{198}+\cdots+\dfrac{x^2}{2}+x+5$, then $g'(0) =$ ____
questions.explanation: $g'(x)=x^{199}+x^{198}+\cdots+x+1$; at $x=0$ only the constant term $1$ survives.

questions.q: $f(x) = \begin{cases}3x-8 & \text{if } x\le5\\ 2k & \text{if } x>5\end{cases}$ is continuous, find $k$.
questions.explanation: Continuity at $x=5$ requires $2k=3(5)-8=7\Rightarrow k=7/2$.

questions.q: If $x = ct$, $y = \dfrac{c}{t}$, find $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ at $t = 2$.
The function $f(x)=[x]$, where $[x]$ denotes greatest integer function is continuous at ____
questions.explanation: $[x]$ is discontinuous only at integers; $1.5$ is not an integer, so it is continuous there.

questions.q: If $y=\log\left(\dfrac{1-x^2}{1+x^2}\right)$, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ is equal to ____
The function represented by the following graph [a V-shaped graph with vertex on the x-axis near x = 1] is
options: Neither continuous nor differentiable at x = 1
Differentiable but not continuous at x = 1
Continuous but not differentiable at x = 1
questions.explanation: A V-shaped graph like |x-1| is continuous everywhere but has a sharp corner (unequal one-sided derivatives) at the vertex x=1.

questions.q: If f(x) = $\begin{cases}\dfrac{3\sin\pi x}{5x} & x\neq0\\ 2K & x=0\end{cases}$ is continuous at x = 0, then the value of K is
questions.explanation: $\lim_{x\to0}\dfrac{3\sin\pi x}{5x}=\dfrac{3\pi}{5}$. For continuity, $2K=\dfrac{3\pi}{5}$, so $K=\dfrac{3\pi}{10}$.

questions.q: Which one of the following is not correct for the features of exponential function given by f(x) = $b^x$ where b > 1?
options: The range of the function is the set of all positive real numbers
The point (1, 0) is always on the graph of the function
The domain of the function is R, the set of real numbers
For very large negative values of x, the function is very close to 0
questions.explanation: The graph of $b^x$ passes through (0,1), not (1,0), so statement (2) is not correct.

questions.q: If y = (1 + x)(1 + $x^2$)(1 + $x^4$), then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ at x = 1 is
questions.explanation: Using product rule at x=1 where each factor equals 2: $y'(1) = 1\cdot2\cdot2 + 2\cdot1\cdot2\cdot2 + 4\cdot1\cdot2\cdot2 = 4+8+16=28$.

questions.q: If y = $(\tan^{-1}x)^2$, then $(x^2+1)^2y_2 + 2x(x^2+1)y_1$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Differentiating twice and simplifying the given combination yields the constant 2.

questions.q: If the function f(x) defined by f(x) = $\dfrac{x^{100}}{100}+\dfrac{x^{99}}{99}+\ldots+\dfrac{x^2}{2}+x+1$, then f'(0) =
questions.explanation: f'(x) = $x^{99}+x^{98}+\ldots+x+1$, so f'(0) equals the constant term = 1.

questions.q: Let $f(x)=\begin{cases}x, & x\text{ is irrational}\\0, & x\text{ is rational}\end{cases}$, then f is
questions.explanation: Near $x=0$ both rational and irrational sequences give function values approaching 0, but at any other point they give different limits, so f is continuous only at $x=0$.

questions.q: If $x+y=\tan^{-1}y$ and $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}=f(y)\dfrac{dy}{dx}$, then $f(y)=$
questions.explanation: Differentiating gives $dy/dx=-(1+y^2)/y^2$; differentiating again shows $f(y)=2/y^3$.

questions.q: $f(x)=\begin{cases}2a-x, & -a<x<a\\3x-2a, & a\le x\end{cases}$. Then which of the following is true?
questions.explanation: The function is continuous at $x=a$ (both pieces equal $a$), but the left derivative $-1$ differs from the right derivative $3$.

questions.q: Let $f(x)=\cos^{-1}\left[\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{13}}(2\cos x-3\sin x)\right]$. Then $f'(0.5)=$
questions.explanation: Writing $2\cos x-3\sin x=\sqrt{13}\cos(x+\phi)$ gives $f(x)=x+\phi$, so $f'(x)=1$ everywhere.

questions.q: If $f(x)$ is a function such that $f''(x)+f(x)=0$ and $g(x)=[f(x)]^2+[f'(x)]^2$ and $g(3)=8$, then $g(8)=$
questions.explanation: $g'(x)=2f'(x)[f(x)+f''(x)]=0$, so g is constant; hence $g(8)=g(3)=8$.

questions.q: If $m\sin^{-1}x = \log_e y$, then $(1 - x^2)y'' - xy' =$
questions.explanation: Differentiating $y=e^{m\sin^{-1}x}$ twice gives the standard differential equation $(1-x^2)y''-xy'-m^2y=0$, so $(1-x^2)y''-xy'=m^2y$.

questions.q: If $y = e^{\log_e[1+x+x^2+\ldots]}$, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx} =$
questions.explanation: $y=1+x+x^2+\ldots=\dfrac{1}{1-x}$ (for $|x|<1$), so $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{1}{(1-x)^2}$. KEA awarded a grace mark for this question, likely because the condition $|x|<1$ for the series to converge was not stated.

questions.q: If $f(x)$ is an even function, then $f'(x)$ is
options: may be even or may be odd
questions.explanation: Differentiating $f(-x)=f(x)$ gives $-f'(-x)=f'(x)$, i.e. $f'(-x)=-f'(x)$, so $f'$ is odd.

questions.q: If $f(x) = \sin[\pi^2]x + \cos[-\pi^2]x$ then $f'(x)$ is, here $[\pi^2]$ and $[-\pi^2]$ greatest integer function not greater than its value
questions.explanation: $[\pi^2]=9$ and $[-\pi^2]=-10$, so $f(x)=\sin9x+\cos10x$ (cosine is even), giving $f'(x)=9\cos9x-10\sin10x$.

questions.q: If $f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{x^2-(a+2)x+a}{x-2}, & x \ne 2 \\ 2, & x = 2 \end{cases}$ is continuous at $x = 2$, then the value of $a$ is
questions.explanation: For the limit at $x=2$ to be finite, $(x-2)$ must divide the numerator, which forces $a=0$; then $f(x)=x$ near $x=2$, and the limit $2$ matches $f(2)$.

questions.q: If $f(x)=\begin{cases}\dfrac{\log x}{x-1} & \text{if }x\neq1\\ k & \text{if }x=1\end{cases}$ is continuous at $x=1$, then the value of $k$ is ............
questions.explanation: $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to1}\dfrac{\log x}{x-1}=1$ (a standard limit), so for continuity $k=1$.

questions.q: If $\sqrt r=ae^{\theta\cot\alpha}$ where $a$ and $\alpha$ are real numbers, then $\dfrac{d^2r}{d\theta^2}-4r\cot^2\alpha$ is ............
questions.explanation: $r=a^2e^{2\theta\cot\alpha}$, so $\dfrac{dr}{d\theta}=2\cot\alpha\cdot r$ and $\dfrac{d^2r}{d\theta^2}=4\cot^2\alpha\cdot r$; hence the expression is $0$.

questions.q: The derivative of $\tan^{-1}\left[\dfrac{\sin x}{1+\cos x}\right]$ with respect to $\tan^{-1}\left[\dfrac{\cos x}{1+\sin x}\right]$ is ............
questions.explanation: $\tan^{-1}\left[\dfrac{\sin x}{1+\cos x}\right]=\dfrac x2$ and $\tan^{-1}\left[\dfrac{\cos x}{1+\sin x}\right]=\dfrac\pi4-\dfrac x2$. The derivative of the first with respect to the second is $\dfrac{1/2}{-1/2}=-1$.

questions.q: $\dfrac{d}{dx}\left[\cos^2\left(\cot^{-1}\sqrt{\dfrac{2+x}{2-x}}\right)\right]$ is ............
questions.explanation: With $\cot\theta=\sqrt{\dfrac{2+x}{2-x}}$, $\cos^2\theta=\dfrac{\cot^2\theta}{1+\cot^2\theta}=\dfrac{2+x}{4}$, whose derivative with respect to $x$ is $\dfrac14$.

questions.q: If $f(x)=\dfrac{\sin^2x}{1+\cot x}+\dfrac{\cos^2x}{1+\tan x}$, then $f'\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$ is ............
questions.explanation: Simplifying, $f(x)=\dfrac{\sin^3x+\cos^3x}{\sin x+\cos x}=1-\sin x\cos x=1-\dfrac12\sin2x$, so $f'(x)=-\cos2x$, and $f'(\pi/4)=-\cos(\pi/2)=0$.

questions.q: If $\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac yb\right)=n\log\left(\dfrac xn\right)$, then .......................
questions.explanation: Differentiating, $\dfrac{-y_1}{\sqrt{b^2-y^2}}=\dfrac nx$, so $xy_1+n\sqrt{b^2-y^2}=0$.

questions.q: If $y=\sin x\cdot\sin2x\cdot\sin3x...........\sin nx$, then $y'$ is ............
questions.explanation: Taking logarithms, $\ln y=\sum\ln(\sin kx)$, so $\dfrac{y'}{y}=\sum k\cot kx$, i.e. $y'=y\cdot\sum_{k=1}^n k\cot kx$.

questions.q: The function $f(x)=|x-2|+x$ is
questions.explanation: $f(x)=2$ for $x<2$ and $f(x)=2x-2$ for $x\ge2$; both pieces agree at $x=2$ (value $2$), so $f$ is continuous everywhere, in particular at $x=0$ and $x=2$, but its derivative jumps from $0$ to $2$ at $x=2$.

questions.q: The function $f(x)=[x]$, where $[x]$ denotes the greatest integer not greater than $x$, is
options: continuous for all real values of $x$.
continuous only at rational values of $x$.
continuous for all nonintegral values of $x$.
continuous only at positive integral values of $x$.
questions.explanation: The greatest integer function has jump discontinuities exactly at integers, so it is continuous everywhere else, i.e. at all nonintegral values of $x$.

questions.q: If the three functions $f(x)$, $g(x)$ and $h(x)$ are such that $h(x)=f(x)\cdot g(x)$ and $f'(x)\cdot g'(x)=c$, where $c$ is a constant, then $\dfrac{f''(x)}{f(x)}+\dfrac{g''(x)}{g(x)}+\dfrac{2c}{f(x)\cdot g(x)}$ is equal to
questions.explanation: $h''=f''g+2f'g'+fg''=f''g+fg''+2c$; dividing by $h=fg$ gives exactly the given expression, so it equals $h''(x)/h(x)$.

questions.q: The derivative of $e^{ax}\cos bx$ with respect to $x$ is $re^{ax}\cos\left(bx+\tan^{-1}\dfrac{b}{a}\right)$. When $a>0, b>0$, the value of $r$ is
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{d}{dx}(e^{ax}\cos bx)=e^{ax}(a\cos bx-b\sin bx)$, which can be written as $\sqrt{a^2+b^2}\,e^{ax}\cos(bx+\tan^{-1}(b/a))$, so $r=\sqrt{a^2+b^2}$.

questions.q: If $x=a\cos^3\theta$ and $y=a\sin^3\theta$, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=$
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{3a\sin^2\theta\cos\theta}{-3a\cos^2\theta\sin\theta}=-\tan\theta=-\sqrt[3]{y/x}$, using $\sin\theta=(y/a)^{1/3}$, $\cos\theta=(x/a)^{1/3}$.

questions.q: If $y=\tan^{-1}\sqrt{x^2-1}$, then the ratio $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}:\dfrac{dy}{dx}=$
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{1}{x\sqrt{x^2-1}}$ and $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}=-\dfrac{2x^2-1}{x^2(x^2-1)^{3/2}}$; their ratio simplifies to $\dfrac{1-2x^2}{x(x^2-1)}$.

questions.q: The function $f(x) = \dfrac{\log(1+ax) - \log(1-bx)}{x}$ is not defined at $x=0$. The value which should be assigned to 'f' at $x=0$ so that it is continuous at $x=0$ is
questions.explanation: As $x\to0$, $\log(1+ax)\approx ax$ and $\log(1-bx)\approx -bx$, so $f(x) \to \dfrac{ax+bx}{x} = a+b$.

questions.q: If $f(x) = 1 + nx + \dfrac{n(n-1)}{2}x^2 + \dfrac{n(n-1)(n-2)}{6}x^3 + \ldots + x^n$, then $f''(1) =$
If $f(x) = \log_{x^2}(\log_e x)$, then $f'(x)$ at $x = e$ is
questions.explanation: Writing $f(x)=\dfrac{\ln(\ln x)}{2\ln x}$ and differentiating gives $f'(x)=\dfrac{1-\ln(\ln x)}{2x\ln^2x}$; at $x=e$, $\ln x=1,\ln(\ln x)=0$, so $f'(e)=\dfrac{1}{2e}$. (Grace marks were awarded to all, likely due to the ambiguous printed base notation.)

questions.q: If $y = \sin^n x \cos nx$, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ is
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = n\sin^{n-1}x\cos x\cos nx - n\sin^n x\sin nx = n\sin^{n-1}x[\cos x\cos nx - \sin x \sin nx] = n\sin^{n-1}x\cos(n+1)x$.

questions.q: If $f(x) = \dfrac{g(x)+g(-x)}{2} + \dfrac{2}{[h(x)+h(-x)]^{-1}}$ where g and h are differentiable functions, then $f'(0)$
questions.explanation: Both $g(x)+g(-x)$ and $h(x)+h(-x)$ are even functions of $x$, so $f(x)$ is even; the derivative of an even function is odd, and an odd function must vanish at $x=0$, so $f'(0)=0$.
